fuzzy.text: Distances are weighted by systematic sound correspondences between dialects, so dialect and spelling differences count as very close — you don't need to know how the other side spells it.
fuzzy.title: Cross-dialect fuzzy search

provenance.text: Page numbers, list rows and recording timecodes are shown; sources with scans let you open the original page, and citations copy in one click.
provenance.title: Every entry is traceable

sources.text: Dictionaries, word lists and recorded corpora are each converted into one standard format by their own adapter, so a single search covers them all.
sources.title: Many sources, one format

field.nativeHint: Word forms, variants, other spellings, and words inside sentences

filter.fuzzinessHint: “Standard” finds cross-dialect sound correspondences and small spelling differences; “Exact” only matches identical normalised spellings. Either way, words that start with or contain your query are also listed.
filter.varietyNote: {child} is a local variety of {parent}; selecting “{parent}” includes it.

group.windowed: {total} in total; showing {window} on either side.

lab.dawgHelp: Each node shows “subtree lower bound / allowed limit”. When the lower bound exceeds the limit the node is pruned and nothing below it is computed. Words in the primary colour are results within the threshold. The bound also accounts for multi-character rules that can span several levels at once, so no result is missed. The DAWG merges shared suffixes, so the same node number may appear under different paths.
lab.dawgSize: Word graph: {nodes} nodes, {edges} edges (a trie of the same words would need many more nodes)
lab.intro: See how the cross-dialect weighted edit distance is computed: ordinary substitutions, deletions and insertions are expensive, while systematic sound correspondences between dialects cost only {rule}. Change the rules and costs and the table and word-graph search update instantly.
lab.introNoRules: See how the weighted edit distance is computed. Change the rules and costs and the table and word-graph search update instantly.
lab.legend: Corner arrows: ↖ match or substitute, ↑ delete, ← insert, ⤡ sound rule (may span several cells). A dot on a column header marks a word-final position where word-final rules apply. Darker cells cost more; highlighted cells form the best path.

cell.match: D({i}, {j}) = {value}: the characters are the same, so D({fromI}, {fromJ}) = {from} carries over.
cell.delete: D({i}, {j}) = {value}: delete an extra character of the query, D({fromI}, {fromJ}) + {stepCost}.
cell.insert: D({i}, {j}) = {value}: insert a character missing from the query, D({fromI}, {fromJ}) + {stepCost}.

note.path: The table is complete; the bottom-right cell is the distance, {distance}. Tracing each cell back to its best source gives the best alignment ({length} steps).

node.open: Visit “{prefix}”: the row’s lower bound {lowerBound} is within the limit {bound}, so the walk continues.
node.pruned: Prune “{prefix}”: lower bound {lowerBound} > limit {bound}, so the whole subtree is skipped.
node.accepted: “{prefix}” is a word at distance {distance}, within the limit {bound}: it is a result.
node.rejected: “{prefix}” is a word, but its distance {distance} exceeds the limit {bound}; closer words may lie below, so the walk continues.

bcdp.levelPrefix: Prefix level {level}: the states of all chains of exactly {level} prefix(es) at their innermost boundary, merged by element-wise minimum; {count} cell(s) are finite. Each level walks the prefix trie once.
bcdp.levelSuffix: Suffix level {level}: from the word end inwards, with the mirrored rules; chains of exactly {level} suffix(es) merged into one row; {count} cell(s) are finite.
bcdp.merge: All prefix levels merge into the start of the stem ({prefix} finite cell(s)); all suffix levels merge into the coupling at the stem’s end ({suffix} finite cell(s)); {crossing} rule(s) are still open and may cross a boundary.

channel.plain: Channel “{text}”: no prefix, so the stem starts at the word start and needs at least one suffix.
channel.prefix: Channel “{text}”: the stem starts from the merged prefix state; it may be followed by suffixes or end the word.
channel.infix: Removing the infix <{form}> gives the restored variant “{text}”; the stem’s start is fixed in the query.
channel.reduplication: Removing the reduplicant “{form}” gives the restored variant “{text}”; the template fixes where the stem starts and how long it is.
channel.circumfix: Channel “{text}”: the stem follows the left part of circumfix {form} and must end with its suffix; both parts count as one step.
channel.circumfixInner: Removing the left part “{left}” of circumfix {form} gives the restored variant “{text}”: the stem start is fixed on the query and the stem must end with the circumfix suffix.

bcdp.walk: Channel “{text}”: shares one walk of the lexicon with plain search; {visited} node(s) visited, {pruned} pruned; at word ends the stem couples with the suffixes, and {found} word(s) are within the limit.
bcdp.hits: {count} root(s) found; only those with cost up to {cutoff} are kept.
bcdp.hit: Best analysis of “{term}”: cost {distance} ({steps} morphological step(s)). The whole-word alignment follows step by step.
bcdp.tooShort: The query is too short: morphological search needs at least one character more than the minimum root length ({minStem}).

miss.same: “{term}” is the query itself, which is a plain fuzzy match.
miss.short: “{term}” is shorter than the minimum root length.
miss.bound: Even the best analysis of “{term}” exceeds the cost limit {maxDistance}.
miss.spread: The cost of “{term}” is above the cutoff {cutoff} (best hit + lemmaSpread), so it is not listed.

lab.prunedReason: Pruned: lower bound over the limit

playback.label: Step-by-step playback
playback.idleDp: Press Play or → to fill the table cell by cell; each cell takes the cheapest of its candidate transitions.
playback.idleDawg: Press Play or → to walk the DAWG node by node; subtrees whose lower bound exceeds the limit are skipped.
playback.idleMorph: Press Play or → to step through the morphological search: prefixes and suffixes level by level, one shared walk of the lexicon, then the whole-word alignment.

morph.error: Could not get the explanation (is the search index still loading?).
morph.empty: Enter a derived word to see how morphological search finds its root.
morph.hits: Roots found ({count}); pick one to see its analysis
morph.cutoff: Only roots with cost up to {cutoff} are listed (best hit + lemmaSpread); whether other roots appear depends on the best hit of the same query.
morph.truncated: Too many restored variants; the rest were truncated.
morph.pickTerm: Pick a root above to see its alignment and analysis.
morph.settingsNote: The morphology tab uses the site’s actual dialect rules and morphology spec; the rule settings only affect the first two tabs.
morph.levels: ① Affix levels and boundary states
morph.levelsLegend: Each cell is the least cost of an alignment that reaches query position x at this morpheme boundary (affix costs included); all chains of one level are merged by element-wise minimum. Suffixes are computed from the word end inwards and shown here in forward positions.
morph.crossing: Rules still open and able to cross a boundary: {prefix} on the prefix side, {suffix} on the suffix side (for example vowel coalescence across a｜a).
morph.channels: ② Channels and the lexicon walk
morph.walkResult: {visited} node(s) visited, {found} word(s) within the limit
morph.alignmentLegend: The query is aligned with the underlying string “affixes · root · affixes”; ｜ marks a morpheme boundary, and rules may cross it.

match.costs: Each sound-correspondence rule costs only {rule}; an ordinary substitution, deletion or insertion costs {substitute} / {delete} / {insert}.
match.costsNoRules: A substitution, deletion or insertion costs {substitute} / {delete} / {insert}.
match.openLab: See the calculation in the algorithm lab →

morph.disclaimer: This result comes from an algorithm that removes affixes automatically. It is meant to make searching easier and is not a verified analysis; please judge whether it is correct.
